**8B.7 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 outcome picture is mixed. On the welfare/economic side, there is real evidence of improvement or stabilization in poverty, labor income, direct benefits, school reach, and health-system access. On the security, rule-of-law, and information-space side, outcomes were clearly worse or still badly deficient. So the strongest read is: **partly yes on social-policy outcomes, no on security and institutional outcomes**.

**Evidence for “yes, in some areas”**
- **Salen de la pobreza laboral 3.2 millones de personas en el último año** | Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social | 2024-09-05 | https://www.gob.mx/stps/prensa/salen-de-la-pobreza-laboral-3.2-millones-de-personas-en-el-ultimo-ano?idiom=es  
  Claim: labor poverty fell to 35.0% in Q2 2024, 3.2 million people exited labor poverty in a year, and real wages/minimum-wage purchasing power rose. This is the clearest outcome-level support for AMLO’s poverty-reduction claim.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Mexico country profile** | World Bank | 2024 | https://pip.worldbank.org/country-profiles/MEX  
  Claim: the World Bank’s 2024 profile shows national poverty at 29.6% and bottom-40 consumption growth outperforming the average, which is consistent with lower-income households doing better. This supports the direction of the administration’s distributive claims, though not uniquely attributable to AMLO.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **IMSS-Bienestar coverage and rollout** | IMSS | 2024-04-17 | https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202404/170  
  Claim: IMSS-Bienestar was operating at large scale with 131,000 workers, 635 hospitals, and 11,913 health centers serving 53.2 million uninsured people. That is strong evidence that the health-access outcome moved in the intended direction.  
  IDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- **La Escuela es Nuestra reaches 99% of basic schools** | Presidencia de México | 2024-06-26 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-escuela-es-nuestra-alcanza-cobertura-del-99-por-ciento-en-planteles-de-educacion-basica/  
  Claim: the school program covered 99% of basic-education campuses and used direct funds through parent committees. This supports the claim that educational access and school conditions improved in a concrete, not just rhetorical, way.  
  IDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Misión cumplida: se consolidan pensiones y programas de bienestar** | Secretaría de Bienestar | 2024-09-04 | https://www.gob.mx/bienestar/prensa/mision-cumplida-se-consolidan-pensiones-y-programas-de-bienestar  
  Claim: 14.4 million people received direct social benefits in 2024, including 12.2 million older adults on the old-age pension. That is substantial evidence of expanded baseline income security for vulnerable groups.  
  IDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- **Mexico 2024 Article IV / FCL review** | IMF | 2024-11-01 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/11/01/mexico-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-review-under-the-flexible-credit-line-arrangement-556997  
  Claim: the IMF said Mexico still had very strong macro frameworks and that inflation pressures were receding, even while warning about procyclical fiscal policy and slowing growth. This is mixed, but it does support a partial “direction moved as claimed” reading on macro stability.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Banxico quarterly report** | Banco de México | 2024-08-28 | https://www.banxico.org.mx/publicaciones-y-prensa/resumenes-visuales/informe-trimestral-html/informe-trimestral-abr-jun-00003.html  
  Claim: Banxico kept policy oriented to the 3% inflation target and only eased as inflation slowed. This supports the claim that the macro framework remained functional and broadly on the intended track.  
  IDs: 8B.7

**Evidence for “no, or not broadly”**
- **Rampant extortion reveals corrosive hole in Mexico security strategy** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rampant-extortion-reveals-corrosive-hole-in-mexico-security-strategy-3283251  
  Claim: extortion remained far above the level when AMLO took office, which undercuts any claim that everyday insecurity was meaningfully solved. This is strong negative outcome evidence.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Mexico: World Report 2024** | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico  
  Claim: HRW said AMLO made little progress on extreme criminal violence, abuses against migrants, gender-based violence, attacks on journalists and defenders, torture, disappearances, and extrajudicial killings. This is broad counterevidence to a strong outcome-improvement story.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Mexico’s sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-15 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588  
  Claim: Reuters said the reform weakened judicial independence and investor confidence. Even if it was a legislative success for AMLO, the outcome for institutions and predictability moved in the wrong direction.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Mexico military’s role in migrant massacre comes under sharp scrutiny** | Reuters | 2024-10-16 | https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-militarys-role-in-migrant-massacre-comes-under-sharp-scrutiny-2024-10-16/  
  Claim: Reuters reported soldiers killed six migrants, with the military account disputed locally. This is direct negative evidence on whether vulnerable people were becoming safer under the state.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **Freedom on the Net 2024: Mexico** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024  
  Claim: Freedom House reported covert military monitoring of critics, inauthentic accounts, and surveillance justified by insecurity with little oversight. That is an adverse outcome for transparency and public-information integrity.  
  IDs: 8B.7

- **UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention visit report** | ONU-DH / UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention | 2024-09-17 | https://hchr.org.mx/relatorias_grupos/visita-a-mexico-informe-del-grupo-de-trabajo-sobre-la-detencion-arbitraria/  
  Claim: arbitrary detention remained widespread and was linked to ill-treatment, torture, disappearances, and arbitrary executions. That is strong evidence that coercive-state outcomes did not move in the claimed safer/lawful direction.  
  IDs: 8B.7

**Synthesis**
- **Best-supported positive direction**: poverty/labor income, direct welfare reach, school coverage, and health-system rollout.
- **Best-supported negative direction**: insecurity, abuse by coercive institutions, judicial independence, and information-space repression.
- **Caution**: several positive items are official self-reports, so they count more as implementation/outcome signals than as independent verification. The strongest independent support comes from labor poverty, World Bank/IMF/Banxico macro data, and the large-scale IMSS-Bienestar / school / pension delivery footprint.
- **Practical read for 8B.7**: **mixed-to-moderately positive on social welfare outcomes, but clearly negative on security and institutional outcomes**.
